trades.headline: Sell Josh Downs and Stefon Diggs for Terry McLaurin and Justin Herbert, your QB fix
trades.summary: You cash in two risers and get a QB upgrade plus a receiver with a bigger role than his results show.

give: Diggs is at 14.8 points per game against a 10.7 projection on 58% of snaps, with two touchdowns in week 2.
Downs' FantasyCalc value is up 56% in 30 days while he scores right on his projection.
get: McLaurin has a 24% target share and 78% of snaps but is at 10.0 points per game against a 12.0 projection; his value is down about 40% in 30 days.
He drew 9 targets and three end-zone looks in week 2, but only 0.7 red-zone looks per game overall.
Herbert is at 14.7 points per game against a 19.8 projection; his value is down 67% in 30 days.
you: Herbert replaces Daniel Jones at QB; McLaurin and Metcalf take the flex spots.
them: ChampaignTornadoes is 1-2 and gets two receivers who are producing now.
The trade is within 8% on FantasyCalc value, in their favor.
experts: Draft Sharks says McLaurin isn't helping fantasy teams yet, which is the low price you are buying.
The Commanders' offensive coordinator has said he wants McLaurin at 10 targets a game, though Diggs' arrival may cap that.

risks: Daniels is out, so the Washington passing game is at risk and McLaurin still shares targets with Diggs.
Herbert is underproducing his projection; this and 1oaelbm are alternatives, not a pair.

trades.headline: Sell TD-fueled Juwan Johnson and Josh Downs for Jalen Hurts, a real QB upgrade on Daniel Jones
trades.summary: You sell two players whose prices jumped this month for a QB who is producing near projection at a discounted price. Schultz and Metcalf fill the spots they leave.

give: Johnson is scoring 16.8 points per game against a 10.2 projection on a 15% target share; his FantasyCalc value is up 200% in 30 days.
Downs' value is up 56% in 30 days, but he is scoring right on his projection (10.9 vs 11.3), so the price has run ahead of the output.
Johnson's 2025 TE10 finish came on volume with only 3 touchdowns; this year he is scoring 60% over projection on a 15% target share.
get: Hurts is at 20.9 points per game against a 22.5 projection with 98% of snaps and 1 red-zone look per game; his FantasyCalc value is down 24% in 30 days.
His price fell on summer worries about a new offense, but he is already producing at about 93% of projection.
you: Jones is at 13.8 points per game against a 16.7 projection and Jayden Daniels is out, so QB is your weakest spot.
Hurts replaces Daniel Jones (FantasyCalc value 130, down 40% in 30 days) at QB, your thinnest spot.
Dalton Schultz moves into the TE slot and DK Metcalf into a flex spot; your lineup value rises about 5.7%.
them: Ben Hur Returns is 1-2 and thin at TE and WR; they get two players producing this month, but they lose their QB and would start Tyler Shough.
The package is within 4% on FantasyCalc value, so they may still balk at losing their QB.
experts: Johnson coverage credits volume rather than touchdowns for last year's finish and flags rookie competition for targets.
Downs is expected to take on a bigger role after the Pittman trade, which is why his value has risen.

risks: Hurts may keep trending up, so his price may not stay this low.
Johnson could keep scoring and the TE spot would then be worse for you.

trades.headline: Sell Juwan Johnson and Stefon Diggs at their peak for Justin Herbert and Tucker Kraft
trades.summary: Two players outscoring their projections turn into a QB1 and a TE who is scoring under his projection while his role holds.

give: Johnson is at 16.8 points per game against a 10.2 projection, with his FantasyCalc value up 200% in 30 days.
Diggs is at 14.8 against a 10.7 projection on only 58% of snaps, with two touchdowns in his week 2 game.
get: Herbert is at 14.7 points per game against a 19.8 projection with 1.3 red-zone looks per game; his FantasyCalc value is down 67% in 30 days (712).
Kraft is at 6.5 against an 11.3 projection with 79% of snaps and a 14% target share; his value is down about 40% in 30 days.
you: Herbert replaces Daniel Jones at QB and Kraft replaces Johnson at TE; Metcalf moves into a flex spot.
them: ChampaignTornadoes is 1-2 and gets two players producing right now in exchange for a QB and TE that have been slow.
The trade is within 5% on FantasyCalc value.
experts: Kraft is back from an ACL tear and has played 79% of snaps through 3 games, so a snap-count limit looks like a small worry.
CBS's preview calls Herbert a QB1 in all leagues, though he is scoring below that so far.

risks: Kraft's 14% target share is low for a TE1 and Herbert is underproducing his projection.
This deal and 9qgi2b both chase Herbert with the same partner and Diggs, so you can only do one.

trades.headline: Move Dalton Schultz and a dead-weight RB for Bo Nix, a low-cost QB upgrade
trades.summary: Schultz is a bench TE whose value jumped 265% in a month; Nix costs less and upgrades your QB spot.

give: Schultz is at 13.2 points per game against a 10.4 projection with a 22% target share, and his value is up 265% in 30 days, but he sits on your bench.
Kenny Gainwell has 42% of snaps and is scoring 3.4 points per game, so he is a spare part for you.
get: Nix is at 18.3 points per game against a 19.3 projection with 100% of snaps and 1.7 red-zone looks per game; his value is down 43% in 30 days.
He rushed for 356 yards and five touchdowns last year, which is where his upside comes from.
you: Nix replaces Daniel Jones at QB; nothing else in your lineup changes.
them: Strikes is thin at QB and RB but deep at TE, so they get a TE upgrade for their QB; they would have to drop Emanuel Wilson.
The trade is within 6% on FantasyCalc value.
experts: RotoBaller noted Nix rebounded in week 2 but has run very little so far, which holds down his upside.
Nix's early schedule is tough, which is why his price is low.

risks: Nix's rushing has been low, which cuts his weekly ceiling.
Denver's schedule stays hard for several more weeks.
